title: Outlook on the web: inline Copilot chat for drafting emails without opening the sidebar
summary: Hold: the access guidance omits that app availability settings do not override existing administrator deployments, so restricting self-installation alone may leave users with access. The data-access explanation also omits the documented Work IQ exception and asserts unchanged data reach without evidence.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans inline chat for Outlook email drafting without opening the Copilot Chat sidebar.
claims.quote: Instead of opening Copilot Chat every time you want to use Copilot to draft a message, this change introduces an inline chat component that streamlines the process and lets you interact with Copilot without opening the sidebar.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe this specific planned inline chat feature.

claims.claim: Feature-specific rollout mechanics, prerequisites, and sidebar replacement details are not stated.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The inline chat default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook Copilot inline chat compose disable policy default licensing November 2026'. Read roadmap and Copilot settings; searched release notes for 570440 and inline chat. No stated default found.

claims.claim: The included licensing model rests on the documented Basic Outlook drafting entitlement, with no inline-specific requirement asserted.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel).
Outlook: Draft emails, summarize threads, and use the coaching tips to improve clarity, sentiment and tone

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) lists Outlook email drafting, thread summaries, and coaching as in-app features.
claims.quote: Outlook: Draft emails, summarize threads, and use the coaching tips to improve clarity, sentiment and tone

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) describes users without the Copilot add-on license who have in-app Copilot capabilities.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) includes everything in Basic.
claims.quote: which includes everything in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic)

claims.claim: Copilot Chat in Outlook is an access surface for Copilot Chat (Basic).
claims.quote:
You can access Copilot Chat (Basic) through:
- `copilot.cloud.microsoft`
- Microsoft Copilot app (web, desktop, mobile)
- Copilot Chat in Outlook and Teams

claims.claim: The overview says Basic can use open Outlook content but not organizational data through Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) can't use organizational data via Microsoft Graph when interacting with Copilot Chat.
claims.fix: After this sentence add: 'Microsoft also documents that Copilot Chat in Outlook can access inbox, calendar, meetings, chats and limited files through lexical indexing without the Copilot add-on; this does not establish the new inline chat's data scope.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/privacy-and-protections#organizational-data.

claims.claim: Premium uses Microsoft Graph automatically, without mentioning the Work IQ configuration exception.
claims.quote: When Work IQ is off, Copilot responses aren't grounded in Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.
claims.fix: Replace 'while Premium uses Microsoft Graph automatically' with 'while Premium can automatically use Microsoft Graph and Work IQ; when Work IQ is off, responses are not grounded in Microsoft Graph and Work IQ'.

claims.claim: The change does not change what Copilot can reach.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook inline Copilot chat email drafting unchanged data access'. Read roadmap, Copilot overview, privacy-and-protections search excerpt and release notes. None states that this specific inline chat preserves the existing data-access scope.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'The roadmap describes a new way to reach Copilot while writing mail in Outlook on the web; it does not specify the inline chat's data-access scope.'

claims.claim: The app block control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote:
Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps.
3. Select the Available Apps list.
4. Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane.
5. Select Block app.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented specifically for blocking the Copilot integrated app itself.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph Integrated Apps Copilot app availability users package block API'. Read Integrated Apps, Manage Copilot Chat and package block; searched Set-OwaMailboxPolicy. No operation identifying the Copilot integrated app block found.

claims.claim: Specific-user self-installation is configured under Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install.
claims.quote:
Scroll down and select Edit Users or select the Users tab in the overview pane.
Specific users/group in the organization can install means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app on their own from the store and use it in the client.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented specifically for the Copilot app's Integrated Apps user-availability selection.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Integrated Apps availability scope users Microsoft Graph API PowerShell block'. Read Integrated Apps, Manage Copilot Chat and package block; no Copilot app user-availability operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The app availability selection decides which users can use Copilot in Outlook, without qualifying existing administrator deployments.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own. Any previous admin deployments made are still be honored.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].governs and its rendered label to 'Which users can self-install and use the Copilot app in Outlook'. Add to its note and the group-scoping prose: 'Availability settings do not affect admin-deployed apps; existing admin deployments remain honored.' Replace the first Before rollout bullet with 'Check both Copilot app availability and existing admin deployments in Integrated Apps; restricting self-installation does not remove admin-deployed access.'

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cited Integrated Apps controls require Global Administrator.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app is tenant-wide and blocks it in Outlook, the Copilot app and the web, including licensed users.
claims.quote: If you block the Copilot app using the Integrated app control, you block the Copilot app tenant-wide across the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat says the Integrated Apps block also blocks Copilot in Teams.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.
claims.fix: After the first sentence add: 'The Integrated Apps documentation differs on Teams: it says the block affects Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application, while Teams continues to honor Teams admin center settings.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook Copilot inline chat compose disable policy default licensing November 2026'. Read Copilot settings; searched Set-OwaMailboxPolicy for Copilot and Draft: no matches. No separate inline switch found.

claims.claim: Copilot audit searches use Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Activities – operation names.

Access Copilot audit logs by using the Microsoft Purview portal and selecting Audit.

To search for specific Copilot or AI application scenarios, use the Activities – operation names field

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start date> -EndDate <end date> -RecordType CopilotInteraction searches Copilot interaction records.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
[-RecordType <AuditRecordType>]
The RecordType parameter filters the log entries by record type.
